title: Cloudflare Tunnel Hostname Demand Inventory
app: OpenWrt, UniFi, Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel, DNS over HTTPS resolvers, and scheduled probes via syslog, APIs, and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=cloudflared:connector
| stats count as requests, values(connector) as connectors by hostname
| sort - requests
description: Uses Cloudflare Tunnel request data telemetry to monitor which hostnames are receiving the most tunneled demand in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for public names that deserve priority when debugging or scaling, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Cloudflare Tunnel request data data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a hourly cadence.
visualization: Hostname inventory sorted by request volume.
grandmaExplanation: It gathers which hostnames are receiving the most tunneled demand so you can spot public names that deserve priority when debugging or scaling before it becomes annoying.
